qs.q:
Statement 1: There are seven obligate categories in hierarchy of taxonomy
Statement 2: Other categories of similar type can be called as intermediate categories
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: The obligate categories are species, genus, family, order, class, division/phylum and kingdom. Sub-categories such as sub-species or varieties are added for clear distinction and are called intermediate categories.

qs.q:
Statement 1: Linnaeus system of animal classification is essentially an artificial system, yet it has become a natural system.
Statement 2: Similarities forming the basis in Linnaeus system are indicative of genetic relationship
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: Linnaeus divided the entire living world into two kingdoms. Animalia lack chlorophyll and cellulosic cell wall and show locomotion; Plantae have chlorophyll and cellulosic cell wall but no locomotion.

qs.q:
Statement 1: Museums are places/institution where preserved plant, animals, artistic and educational material are exhibited to public
Statement 2: Museums are of different kinds, like art, history, science and general museum which exhibit their material to public awareness
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: Museums are sources of ancient and present informational matter where preserved plants, animals and artistic and educational material are exhibited for public awareness; they can be categorised into different kinds.

qs.q:
Statement 1: The scientific name Malus malus is illegitimate
Statement 2: It is a tautonym.
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: The scientific name Malus malus is illegitimate because it is just a tautonym.

qs.q:
Statement 1: Death is considered as the regulatory process on earth
Statement 2: It avoids increasing population caused by continuous reproduction
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: Death (stoppage of all life activities, accompanied by an increase in entropy) is compensated by reproduction.

qs.q:
Statement 1: Hierarchial system of classification is useful to reduce volume's description in a catalogue of organism
Statement 2: Characters of a larger category (like division are not repeated for smaller/lower categories family and order)
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: Hierarchy in classification reduces the volume of description in a catalogue of plants and animals: species share more similarities than a genus, genera with common characters form a family, families form an order, orders a class, and classes a phylum.

qs.q:
Statement 1: “The Biological Species” concept helps us to ask how species are formed.
Statement 2: The concept of biological species focusses our attention on the question of how reproductive isolation comes about
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: Ernst Mayr proposed the biological species concept: a group of actually or potentially inter-breeding natural populations which are reproductively isolated from other such groups.

qs.q:
Statement 1: All white tigers in the world are progeny of white male tiger ‘Mohan’
Statement 2: A white male tiger was captured from forest by Maharaja of Rewa and reared as Mohan
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: Almost all white tigers of the world have a common ancestor: a white male tiger captured by the king of Rewa, domesticated at Govindgarh Palace and named ‘Mohan’.

qs.q:
Statement 1: A morphology based approach to taxonomy is called ‘Alpha taxonomy’ and it is old fashioned
Statement 2: A multi-disciplinary approach to taxonomy called ‘Omega taxonomy’ if favored in recent years, as it excludes morphological features.
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: Turrill used alpha taxonomy for collection and identification of organisms on the basis of gross morphology. Omega taxonomy (biosystematics) uses evolutionary, genetic AND morphological traits, so it does not exclude morphological features: Statement 2 is false.

qs.q: Match the following columns

Statement 1: The fungi are widespread in distribution and they even live on or inside other plants and animals
Statement 2: Fungi are able to grow anywhere on land, water or on other organisms because they have a variety of pigments, including chlorophyll, carotenoids fucoxanthin and phycoerythrin.
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: Fungi are widespread (epiphytic, saprophytic, symbiotic, parasitic) but lack chlorophyll and the autotrophic mode of nutrition, so Statement 2 is false.

qs.q:
Statement 1: Euglena is a plant due to presence of chlorophyll.
Statement 2: Euglena cannot be classified on the basis of two kingdom system.
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: Euglena is a green, single-celled organism that moves like animals. Some taxonomists placed it in plants (chlorophyll), others in animals (flagellar locomotion), so it cannot be fitted into the two-kingdom system. It is not a plant: Statement 1 is false.

qs.q:
Statement 1: The true nucleus is generally absent in E. coli and other prokaryotes.
Statement 2: An undifferentiated, unorganized fibrillar nucleus without any limiting membrane is observed in prokaryotic cells.
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: E. coli is a well studied prokaryote. Prokaryotic cells lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; the genetic material lies in the cytoplasm as an unorganised fibrillar nucleus without nuclear membrane (nucleoid).

qs.q:
Statement 1: In fungi, sexual apparatus decreases in complexity from lower to higher forms.
Statement 2: In algae, sexual apparatus increases in complexity from simple to the higher forms.
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: In fungi there is gradual simplification and ultimate elimination of the sexual apparatus from lower to higher forms; in algae it increases in complexity from simple to higher forms.

qs.q:
Statement 1: Viruses cause diseases and replicate when they are in the host
Statement 2: Viruses do not replicate outside the host but they remain alive.
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: Viruses replicate only inside a living host; outside the host they behave as non-living particles, so Statement 2 is false.

qs.q:
Statement 1: Euglena is a plant due to the presence of chlorophyll
Statement 2: Euglena can not be classified on the basis of two kingdom system
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: Euglena is a green, single-celled organism that moves like animals. Some taxonomists included it in plants on the basis of chlorophyll, others in animals with flagellated protozoans because of locomotion by flagella.

qs.q:
Statement 1: Both apospory and apogamy are observed in Pteris.
Statement 2: They are evident by the production of haploid sporophyte by apospory and diploid gametophyte by apogamy.
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: Apospory is development of diploid gametophytes from vegetative parts of the diploid sporophyte without spores; apogamy is development of sporophyte directly from the gametophyte without sex organs and gametes. Statement 2 reverses these, so it is false.

qs.q:
Statement 1: Red algae contributes in producing coral reefs.
Statement 2: Some red algae secrete and deposit calcium carbonate over their walls.
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: In coralline red algae the cell walls become hardened with calcium carbonate; these are important for coral reef formation.

qs.q:
Statement 1: In class-Rhodophyceae, cell wall is made up of cellulose
Statement 2: In class-Rhodophyceae flagellar number is two and position of insertion is lateral
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: Statement 1 is true but Statement 2 is false: in Rhodophyceae flagella are absent.

qs.q:
Statement 1: Fertilization in Cycas in called zooidogamy
Statement 2: Fertilization in Cycas takes place by the formation of pollen tube.
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: Cycas is a gymnosperm in which fertilization is called zooidogamy. A pollen tube is formed through which the male nucleus passes.

qs.q:
Statement 1: In Spirogyra, some cells in one of the two filaments become empty after conjugation.
Statement 2: The aplanogametes from the cells of one filament pass through the conjugation tubes into the cells of the other filament.
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: In Spirogyra conjugation, one cell (gametangium) functions as female and receives the aplanogamete (non-flagellated mass of protoplasm) of the adjacent cell; this transfer leaves behind an empty cell.

qs.q:
Statement 1: Certain marine brown and red algae produce large amounts of hydrocolloids
Statement 2: Algin and carrageenin are used commercially as water holding substance
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: Certain marine brown and red algae produce hydrocolloids (water holding substances), e.g. algin (brown algae) and carrageenan (red algae), which are used commercially. Both statements are true.

qs.q:
Statement 1: Conjugation is a temporary union between two ciliates belonging to two different mating types for the exchange and reconstitution of nuclear materials.
Statement 2: Conjugation occurs between two inactive individuals which have gained their vigour and vitality due to chromosomal imbalance in their macronuclei, caused by repeated amitotic division.
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: In ciliates two individuals fuse temporarily, exchange micronuclear material and separate. Conjugation occurs between individuals that have LOST vigour, so Statement 2 is false.

qs.q:
Statement 1: One male gamete fuses with egg to form zygote
Statement 2: This event is called syngamy
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: Syngamy is the fusion of male and female gametes resulting in formation of a zygote, which develops into a new organism.

qs.q:
Statement 1: The life cycle of Funaria is called diplohaplontic.
Statement 2: In Funaria, there is alternation of haploid gametophytic and diploid sporophytic phases, one becoming parent of the other.
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: In Funaria there are two distinct individuals: the haploid, independent, leafy moss plant and the diploid, leafless sporogonium, partially dependent on the gametophyte for nutrition.

qs.q:
Statement 1: Bryophytes are the amphibians of plant kingdom
Statement 2: They are found in swamps and the areas, where water and land meet
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: Bryophytes live in the transitional (amphibious) zone between aquatic and terrestrial habitats and cannot complete their life cycle without external water; hence they are called amphibians of the plant kingdom.

qs.q:
Statement 1: The term Bryophyta was used first time by Brawn (1864)
Statement 2: He included algae, fungi, lichens and mosses in bryophytes
o: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True; Statement 2 is not correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
qs.s: The term bryophyte was coined by Braun (1864), who included algae, fungi, lichens and mosses. Later algae, fungi and lichens were placed in Thallophyta, while liverworts and mosses stayed in bryophytes.
